title: protect.js: expected Protect failures are reported with core.setFailed and return, not thrown
answers: Protect check shows a stack trace instead of a clear error message
Protect job retries or crashes when no workflow runs are found or checks fail
How do I make the protect workflow fail gracefully with a readable Actions error?
Why does the approval/protect job throw an Error instead of calling core.setFailed?
body:
Symptom: The Protect check fails with a raw exception (or appears to retry) when a required check fails, no workflow runs are found, or the wait times out, instead of a clear Actions error message.
Root cause: .github/workflows/protect.js:module.exports (the async handler) used `throw new Error(...)` for expected outcomes (missing runs, a failed sibling check, timeout).
Fix pattern: For expected outcomes call `core.setFailed(message)` then `return`; keep the polling loop and status reporting unchanged. Null-check the value returned by `fetchChecks` (`if (!checks) return;`) so an expected failure inside the helper exits cleanly.
Constraints: Only expected failures move to setFailed. Unexpected GitHub API errors must still propagate as thrown errors. Keep the script timeout shorter than the job's `timeout-minutes` (reviewer noted the runner would otherwise cancel the job before the script could report "Timeout"); the PR's final value for that constant is not confirmed by the diff.
applies: Applies to .github/workflows/protect.js and similar actions/github-script handlers that gate merges; does not apply to genuine programming or API errors.
says: The merge protection check shows an unhandled crash stack trace instead of a clear error.
Pull request protection job should fail gracefully with a readable message when checks fail.
Protection check crashes on timeout instead of reporting an expired waiting period.
Display user-friendly failure explanations in the merge gate when required validations fail.
search: Expected merge-gate failures in .github/workflows/protect.js must be reported using core.setFailed and a return rather than throwing an Error. Applies to actions/github-script merge gate handlers handling missing runs, sibling check failures, and timeouts, requiring null-checks on fetchChecks. Unexpected GitHub API errors must still propagate as thrown errors, and script timeouts must remain shorter than the runner timeout-minutes.
